label: Tutorial: Rule
description: Steps of the Tutorial button on the Rule page (endpoint rule.detail_rule). A step: target (CSS selector, empty = centred card), title, text (blank line = new paragraph, **bold**, `code`), roles (optional: anonymous, user, member, admin, perm:<key>), demo (rule / bundle: example shown when the target is missing, e.g. an empty list).

steps.title: One rule, everything about it
steps.text: Its content, where it comes from, what it detects, what the community thinks of it — and the tabs below for its history, bundles, similar rules and tests.

steps.title: The rule's pages
steps.text: Each tab is a page about this rule; the steps below go through them.

steps.title: Suggest an edit
steps.text: Not your rule? Propose a change: its owner reviews it and accepts it or not.

steps.title: Proposals
steps.text: Edit proposals sent for this rule, open or closed.

steps.title: History
steps.text: Every version of the rule, with the differences between them.

steps.title: Similarity
steps.text: Rules whose content is close to this one — duplicates or variants.

steps.title: Bundles
steps.text: The bundles that contain this rule.

steps.title: Linked rules
steps.text: Rules this one needs (dependencies) or is related to.

steps.title: Samples
steps.text: Results of the rule on sample sets: detections, misses, false positives.

steps.title: AI analysis
steps.text: Rulezy's review of the rule: what it detects, weaknesses, suggestions.

steps.title: What the rule says about itself
steps.text: References, author and dates read from the rule's own text.

steps.title: Tags
steps.text: TLP / PAP sharing levels, malware families, platforms… Click one to see every rule with it.

steps.title: ATT&CK techniques
steps.text: The MITRE ATT&CK techniques this rule detects. Each opens its page with every rule for it.

steps.title: The rule
steps.text: The rule itself, highlighted, ready to copy.

steps.title: Other views
steps.text: The rule as JSON (all its fields), or as a MISP object when a MISP instance is connected.

steps.title: Actions
steps.text: Everything you can do with this rule, in one bar.

steps.title: Vote and favorite
steps.text: Votes tell others whether the rule works. Logged-in users can vote and keep the rule in their favorites.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: The rule as a file, as JSON, or with the rules it depends on.

steps.title: Source
steps.text: Open the rule in the Git repository it comes from.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Something wrong (stolen, broken, dangerous)? Tell the administrators.

steps.title: Contributors
steps.text: Everyone who wrote or improved this rule.

steps.title: In bundles
steps.text: Bundles that already use this rule.

steps.title: Related rules
steps.text: Other rules from the same source or author.

steps.title: Visualization
steps.text: A graph of the rule and what it is linked to.

steps.title: Quality score
steps.text: A score from the rule's syntax, metadata, references and the community's votes. The (?) explains how it is computed.

steps.title: Discussion
steps.text: Ask a question, report a false positive or thank the author. Logged-in users can comment and react.
